title: Distinguish scratch-directory refusals from invalid PowerShell cache files in docs
outcome: Clarify the Windows cache startup refusal wording so it separately describes invalid scratch ancestors and a cache entry that is not a regular file.
acceptance: The launcher documentation says that linked or non-directory scratch ancestors are refused, and separately says that an existing cache entry must be a regular file, including refusal when it is a directory.
The prose retains the documented startup reasons and preserved run metadata/stage behavior, with no runtime change, cache disabling, cleanup or ignore entry.
